quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Just one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, how should they do it?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle to control it properly?

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back on the seat that you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle instead of holding you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake in a straight line?

options.text: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes together. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Laced-up boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
Speed up to accommodate the one rider.
Split up and have every rider travel as fast or as slow as they want.
Let the rider that wants to go faster lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them ride ahead. Plan to meet at a specific location later.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space?

options.text: Should reduce their usual space cushions by half.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should maintain adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, signal your intentions clearly, and watch for hazards. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you. Keep adequate space around your motorcycle and scan ahead for dangers.

questions.question: How do you operate the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up may only make the danger worse.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Gently roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: What should you do to make yourself more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on all the time. Wear bright or reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to stay visible.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Push up to shift to a higher gear. Push down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist's cushion of space be managed?

options.text: Should vary according to riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should vary according to riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop, the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy and drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what is the best way to stop?

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handle grips firmly and ease off the throttle. Gradually brake on the tire that is not flat if you know which one it is. Slowly move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They alert you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
The driver will always properly yield to you.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to assume a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way. They should hold onto the passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on most motorcycles?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handlebar
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlebar. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: Why is riding directly next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the driver's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing you both.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When is a large following distance not necessary?

options.text: When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. You need more space when the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.
